speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a pruritic rash on your bilateral upper extremities; can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if they have changed in appearance over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the rash has persisted for five months and fluctuates in intensity, have you noticed any specific triggers like heat, sweating, or stress that seem to make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming the absence of fever or joint pain. To further evaluate the chronic, fluctuating nature of your rash, have you noticed any specific patterns regarding the distribution of the lesions (e.g., flexural vs. extensor surfaces) or any associated skin thickening?

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy_Upper_Exremities

speaker: Doctor
text: The skin biopsy and dermoscopy results show normal readings, which helps rule out primary dermatoses like eczema or psoriasis. Given the 5-month history of a pruritic rash on the upper extremities with no fever, joint pain, or recent illness, have you noticed any specific foods, clothing materials, or environmental exposures that seem to trigger the itching?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No history of serious illness. No known drug allergies. Takes no medications. Social history: College student studying graphic design. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Urticaria (Chronic Spontaneous or Physical Urticaria) secondary to a systemic autoimmune condition or drug reaction (despite denial), given the chronic, pruritic, bilateral upper extremity rash with normal biopsy/dermoscopy and no infectious signs. Further workup for autoimmune causes is indicated.
